function.name: cmd_controller_execute
function.description: Executes a system-level command using os.system() on Windows operating systems. It can execute single or multiple commands chained with '&&'. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

command.description: The system command to be executed. To execute multiple commands, separate them with '&&'. For example, 'dir && echo done'.

unit.description: Specifies the unit of measure for the command if applicable. This is not utilized by os.system() directly but can be used for logging or analysis purposes.

message.reasoning: The user asks: "is any vpn is installed". They want to know if any VPN is installed. We need to check if any VPN software is installed on the system. We can use the cmd_controller_execute tool to run a command that checks for installed VPNs. On Windows, we could query installed programs via WMIC or PowerShell. For example, we can run a PowerShell command: Get-WmiObject -Class Win32_Product | Where-Object {$_.Name -match "VPN"} or use Get-ItemProperty HKLM:\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Uninstall\* etc. But we need to return the result. Let's construct a command that lists installed programs containing "VPN" in their name. Use PowerShell: powershell -Command "Get-ItemProperty HKLM:\\Software\\Microsoft\\Windows\\CurrentVersion\\Uninstall\\* | Select-Object DisplayName, DisplayVersion | Where-Object { $_.DisplayName -like '*VPN*' }". That will output lines. We'll pass that as command. Also maybe include 64-bit registry path: HKLM:\\SOFTWARE\\Wow6432Node\\Microsoft\\Windows\\CurrentVersion\\Uninstall\\*. We'll combine them. So command: powershell -Command "(Get-ItemProperty HKLM:\\Software\\Microsoft\\Windows\\CurrentVersion\\Uninstall\\*).DisplayName, (Get-ItemProperty HKLM:\\Software\\Wow6432Node\\Microsoft\\Windows\\CurrentVersion\\Uninstall\\*).DisplayName | Where-Object { $_ -like '*VPN*' }". Actually better: powershell -Command "Get-ItemProperty HKLM:\\Software\\Microsoft\\Windows\\CurrentVersion\\Uninstall\\*, HKLM:\\Software\\Wow6432Node\\Microsoft\\Windows\\CurrentVersion\\Uninstall\\* | Where-Object { $_.DisplayName -like '*VPN*' } | Select-Object DisplayName, DisplayVersion". We'll call that. Then we can parse output. We'll just return the raw output.
